messages:
maya: Posted a draft PRD for the incremental access model + scoped API keys: https://docs.google.com/draft/INCR-ACCESS (please skim). Looking for acceptance criteria, edge cases, and rollout gating. TL;DR: scoped tokens that can be bound to org, project, and optional role claims; backward-compatible with current API keys; support token rotation and revocation.

raj: :eyes: quick Q — for cross-project services (single service talking to multiple projects) do we expect one token per project or a multi-scope token? Customer ask from BetaCorp was explicit about single token for multi-project pipelines.

ana: For acceptance criteria proposal: 1) scoped token can be issued with exactly one of {org, project} or both (org+project = project-scoped but validated under org) 2) API rejects token missing required scope for route (403) 3) admin rotation API invalidates active tokens within 2s of revocation event (propagated across regions) 4) migration mode: existing API keys remain functional under a compatibility flag for 90 days 5) audit-log entries for issue/rotate/revoke include actor, token-id, reason.

liam: Edge case: project deletion -> what happens to tokens issued to that project? We should auto-revoke and surface a delta in the audit logs and to the project's owners. Also consider orphaned long-lived tokens used by CI jobs. Need customer migration docs.

maya: @raj on multi-project tokens — I'd prefer we support a multi-scope token but make it opt-in via `multi_project=true` flag and require justification + audit annotation at creation time. For BetaCorp we can suggest creating service accounts per project in docs.

raj: Sounds reasonable. For token format can we keep short opaque ids plus metadata in KVS so we can rotate without touching clients? Example header: `Authorization: Bearer rk_abc123` and token metadata stored as `token_id` -> {scopes, created_by, expires_at, policy_hash}.

ana: +1 on opaque id. Also we need to define acceptance tests: unit + integration + chaos. Integration test idea: 1) issue project token, call endpoint with and without correct X-Project header, validate 403/200; 2) revoke token, ensure subsequent calls 401; 3) simulate region failover and confirm revocation converges within SLO.

liam: More edge cases: 1) tokens issued with TTL > 365 days (we should cap), 2) role escalations mid-lifetime (if role mapping changes, tokens should reflect policy on next use? or require rotate?), 3) tokens created before org rename / id changes.

maya: Proposed acceptance criteria additions: - TTL max 365d, renewals require re-auth, - role mapping change doesn't retroactively escalate existing tokens (tokens inherit policy at creation) but if policy is tightened we should be able to enforce revocation via policy version increments, - deleting org/project triggers soft-revoke then hard-revoke after 7 days.

sre-bot: Incident policy check: revocation SLO target set to 5s for hosted API, 30s for dedicated customers (due to cache TTLs). Flagged: dedicated customers may need a manual flush step.

raj: For rollout: I suggest staged rollout across modes — first internal staging, then hosted beta (opt-in tenants), then dedicated pilot customers, then default for all hosted. Private deployments get feature via package upgrade with migration script. Rollout gating: no high-severity auth regressions in beta for 2 weeks and revocation SLO met <10s in 99th.

ana: Can we include data migration checklist: export existing API keys -> map to token objects, attach compatibility flag, notify owners, run TTL enforcement job. Add a CLI command `redwood migrate-keys --compat-window=90d`.

liam: Test harness note: add fake project-delete event to e2e to ensure revocation path. Also include a tool to enumerate tokens per project so customers can find orphaned tokens.

maya: I'll update the PRD with these items and drop in an acceptance-criteria checklist. Next steps: please add short bullets inline on the doc (comments enabled). If you have bandwidth, annotate the migration steps and the revocation SLO justification. Planning meeting Fri 09:30 PT to lock rollout plan. :thumbsup:

raj: Commented on docs with sample token API.

ana: Added integration tests and CLI migration stub to the draft.

liam: Will write the project-deletion e2e case and token-enumeration script.

sre-bot: Reminder: deploy window Fri 10:00-14:00 PT, please post final PRD before Fri 08:00 PT to allow ops review.
